heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for professional image generation, video creation, and multimodal visual production.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected premium hero: a full-bleed orange mesh background with a centered-left content block over a layered dashboard collage on the right, combining poster frames, a video timeline, and result cards. Keep the CTA in brand accent orange, add subtle grid lines and orb accents, and treat the media as a stacked product montage rather than a single image. This should feel cinematic yet operational, with enterprise trust conveyed through clean panels, motion chips, and dense proof rather than decorative AI visuals.

repetitionBreakers: Hero uses split media-forward composition; trust uses a tight marquee strip; product area switches to alternating spotlight-plus-grid and accordion-with-visual; testimonials use a carousel instead of a grid; pricing becomes comparison-led; form is centered-card to reset rhythm before final CTA.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image & Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Generate high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore image creation, native audio-video generation, proof, pricing, and a Get started CTA.

sections.backgroundTreatment: bold brand block with subtle overlay grid and floating output previews
sections.designNote: Hero is content-first but visually dynamic: headline answers what it is, subheadline answers who it is for, and the right side shows a layered montage of image outputs, storyboard frames, and a playback timeline. Primary CTA must be exactly 'Get started' and appear in accent color at full opacity. Keep it premium, direct, and above-the-fold expressive.

Immediate credibility after the hero. Use 3-6 recognizable logos in a compact marquee strip. Keep it prominent but not heavy. If actual logos are unavailable, use a metric strip fallback. No CTA here.

Alternate the two product blocks for rhythm: Seedream 4.5 opens as a spotlight-plus-grid module with a large preview pane and supporting capability tiles; Seedance 1.5 Pro follows as an accordion-with-visual on a dark surface to create stronger contrast and emphasize motion/audio sync. Focus only on the click-driving features: image fidelity, multimodal editing, text rendering, audio-video generation, and speed. Avoid a generic feature dump.

Use this as a trust-reinforcement block only if needed for marketplace confidence, but keep it lean and utility-driven. Present as a small card grid or counters on a dark section for visual reset. Since include=false and no points are provided, this can be omitted in implementation or rendered as a minimal spacer if the template requires it.

Show the two starting-at pricing options as a comparison-led decision section. Make it clear and enterprise-oriented rather than promotional. Keep the layout structured and easy to scan, with one plan visually emphasized if necessary. CTA buttons must still read exactly 'Get started' and remain solid accent.

Because there are 4+ testimonials, use a carousel. Keep it proof-rich but not crowded. Mix creative director, video producer, art director, and marketer quotes to reinforce both image and video credibility. Use a slightly lighter, editorial presentation to break away from the pricing block.

End with a centered lead card that feels decisive and low-friction. This is the final conversion moment: title should frame seeing it in action, not signing up. Use a single primary button labeled exactly 'Get started', full-width on mobile, solid accent only.

Optional footer-style media/logo strip if additional brand credibility is needed. Keep it subtle and horizontal, not competing with the form. If used, it should feel like an afterword rather than a second trust bar.

blueprint.designPersonality: A premium, product-led AI dashboard with strong brand orange, enterprise trust, and gallery-driven proof. It feels intelligent, structured, and high-value rather than flashy, with the trust bar and logos acting as the dominant credibility signal. The overall tone is confident, modern, and interactive, built for marketers and creative teams who want speed, control, and professional output.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a layered hero composite showing AI-generated poster-quality images, storyboard frames, and a video timeline preview. Include a second-fold gallery grid with high-fidelity sample outputs, floating labels for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro, and dashboard-like proof chips. Prefer PNG for UI/product visuals and JPEG for hero imagery. Use SVG for icons, badges, and trust marks. If real media is unavailable, construct polished CSS-based visual shells with frame counters, prompt chips, playback bars, and result cards.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The hero headline is long and product-specific, so 40px keeps it balanced, premium, and readable without crowding the layout.

colours.colourReason: The palette is derived exclusively from the brand data: orange for the hero background and primary CTA, white for clarity, charcoal for authority, and soft grey for separation. This creates a distinct, brand-true identity while keeping the page premium and highly legible.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Split hero with brand/logo lockup at top, prominent single-column headline block, short supporting paragraph, and a compact bullet-style benefit list. Primary visual emphasis is on text hierarchy rather than imagery.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Intro hero, then a lead-capture form section immediately below, followed by dense product feature sections. Layout favors vertically stacked content blocks with strong separation rather than long continuous scrolling panels.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Structured form card and content blocks with straightforward rectangular containers, minimal ornamentation, and utility-first spacing. No evidence of glassmorphism or elevated decorative cards.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA appears in the hero as a high-emphasis action; secondary conversion is a form-based request/demo pattern in a dedicated section. CTAs are direct, task-oriented, and repeated at section level rather than in a persistent bar.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern present in the reference.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not visible in the provided reference; infer a standard utility footer if needed, but no footer pattern can be extracted.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Logo-led header with no dominant hero media visible in the extracted portion. Visual strategy relies on typography, icons, and section structure rather than imagery, video, or media panels.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Product sections are vertically stacked feature blocks with a section label, headline, descriptive paragraph, and a list of capability items. Each product can include its own localized CTA and a feature list with short explanatory rows.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form card placed high on the page, visually separated from hero content. Uses hidden fields and a compact conversion flow, implying a short, friction-reducing lead-gen pattern.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static presentation with no visible motion system in the provided markup. Any interactivity appears to be limited to form handling and standard page scripting.
designNotes: Conversion-first structure with immediate lead capture below the hero.
Strong information density suited to B2B and enterprise audiences.
Prioritizes clarity, hierarchy, and quick scanning over immersive storytelling.
Minimal visual decoration suggests a utilitarian, trust-oriented design system.
Suitable for product pages where multiple offerings need clear separation and repeated conversion opportunities.

mustHaveMoments: Prominent hero with clear positioning for both Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro

Gallery or visual demo section in the second fold
Separate capability blocks for image generation and video generation

avoidPatterns: Long abstract brand storytelling before showing product value
Overloading the hero with too many feature bullets
Using a single CTA that only supports self-serve purchase when the intent is demo-led
Dense technical copy without visual proof
Generic AI marketing aesthetics without concrete product differentiation
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is for a complex, high-consideration AI creative solution aimed at professionals and enterprises, so the conversion path should prioritize demo booking over direct purchase. The audience is solution-aware and wants proof of quality, control, and reliability, which makes product-led structure the best fit. Since the visitor trusts logos most, logo-first trust handling must be the dominant credibility device, ideally surfaced immediately after or within the hero. A split hero is best because the page needs to communicate two related products clearly while still keeping the message concise. The visual strategy should emphasize the product and output quality rather than the form, with the gallery placed in the second fold to quickly show image/video capabilities. CTA intensity should be medium: strong enough to drive demo/quote actions, but not overly aggressive given the enterprise context and longer decision cycle.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
